A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Chamfer Guidance work. Their complete main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation, geographic-diversity, downstream classification, and ablation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline evaluations, a feature-extractor ablation, and a human study reporting 965 judgments.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 retain the same feature-space Chamfer objective, DDIM approximation, and inference-time gradient guidance. Retrieval and self-bootstrapping are proposed only as future extensions; the new extractor ablation does not change the method.

E1.justification: Existing image datasets and classification benchmarks are retained. v2 adds human preference assessment and an object-only GeoDE scenario using prompts such as 'a photo of a car,' extending the earlier region-conditioned evaluation without introducing another image dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1a adds Limited Interval guidance and Particle Guidance to the LDM1.5 comparison. Existing comparators remain, and these two additions do not appear in the corresponding LDM3.5M table.

E3.justification: New Appendix C introduces reference-grounded comparisons of generated image sets, collecting 965 judgments from more than twenty annotators. Appendix F adds an LDM1.5 extractor comparison on object-only GeoDE prompts with k=2,4,8,16. Previously reported evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused DINOv2-versus-CLIP ablation examining scaling with exemplar count, plus human validation of perceived correspondence to reference images. Existing guidance-strength, CFG, exemplar-scaling, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, v2 reports uncertainty for an empirical outcome: 92% ± 2% human preference in Appendix C. The meaning and calculation of ±2% are unspecified. No repeated-run or seed information is added for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: Retained numerical results are unchanged. Additions include Limited Interval and Particle Guidance F1 scores of 0.708 and 0.719 in Table 1a, the human preference result, and Table 10's extractor results. In the new GeoDE setting, DINOv2 and CLIP obtain F1=0.7527 and 0.4088 at k=16; these are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under a retained setting.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and sampling equations in Section 3, together with the efficiency calculations in Appendix A, are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims about training-free exemplar guidance, quality and diversity, scaling, downstream accuracy, and 31% FLOPs savings. The shortened conclusion preserves the principal contribution and headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly states a class-conditional applicability limitation and discusses retrieval-based and synthetic-exemplar extensions. Appendix F hypothesizes that CLIP's concept-oriented pretraining encourages average object representations, whereas DINOv2 preserves instance details. Appendix C interprets human preference as corroborating automated evaluations.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new extractor experiment's model, example prompt, and exemplar-count settings, and Figure 3 supplies an example human-study question and interface. Existing software, hardware, training details, and resource links and licenses are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the references add Corso et al.'s Particle Guidance and Kynkäänniemi et al.'s limited-interval guidance, briefly explaining their diversity mechanisms. The broader positioning relative to prior guidance and fine-tuning methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 compresses the conclusion, lightly edits existing prose, expands limitations, and inserts a user-study appendix section. Author and affiliation text, the conference footer, and acknowledgments are updated; most wording and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains two rows, and v2 adds the user-study screenshot as Figure 3 and the extractor comparison as Table 10. Existing plots and qualitative panels are retained, with limited resizing, relocation, and page reflow; old Figures 3–6 become Figures 4–7.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides modest additional checks through two relevant baselines, human judgments, and a targeted extractor ablation. These strengthen empirical support without changing the central findings. The gains are limited by undefined user-study uncertainty and Table 10's misleading lower-FID claim: CLIP actually has lower FID than DINOv2 at every matched k.
